resources.string: Try a prompt in Chat or Compare and you will see the latency, speed and cost of each engine here.
Average total time from sending the prompt until the last word of the answer arrives.
Percentiles: p50 = half of the runs were faster than this value. p95 = 95% of them were. They show consistency, not just the average (a tier with a p95 much higher than its p50 is \"unpredictable\").
Characters of the answer generated per second, on average.
Number of tokens (units of text the model processes, not exactly words) in the answer. Real when the backend exposes it (MediaPipe, Cloud); approximate (characters/4) on ML Kit Nano.
How many of the runs against this tier finished without error, out of the total.

MediaPipe and LiteRT-LM only: how long the model takes to load the first time after opening the app or switching engines. It is kept separate and is NOT added to latency or speed, so that comparing speeds does not mix \"loading\" with \"generating\" (runs saved before this version do have it added in, unseparated).
In Compare you can pick which one answered best. Here you see in how many voted rounds each engine won, out of those it took part in: it is your preference, the complement to the objective metrics.

Only Cloud and Firebase AI (the cloud tiers) show it — on-device ones call no paid API, they cost $0. It is computed with the public Gemini Flash price (input/output) and an approximation of prompt tokens (characters/4, there is no exact input count); treat it as an order of magnitude, not a real bill.
